reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes an automated PancakeSwap front-running bot with claims of “Auto 10x BNB Profit” and potentially more than 1,000 BNB per day. It instructs viewers to fund MetaMask, deploy and transfer BNB to the contract, and activate the process while claiming that 90% of profits will return to the wallet. The video also acknowledges that fees can exceed returns and does not independently verify the contract’s behavior, claimed profits, or resulting loss.

we're just gonna send some funds to that contract
Next thing that we do, after it's sent to the contract, we'll just go over here and press the action button
It automatically buys and sells for you.
it will front-run all the retail investors that come in

opening.argument: Judge, read the profit claims alongside the creator's explicit warning that the contract can lose money to fees. The description says a small funding amount may be consumed by gas and token burn fees, and it gives a funding recommendation in response. That is a material qualification, not a presentation of returns as cost-free or assured. The speaker also calls the reported results personal experience and offers transaction reports as potential corroboration. Those statements do not prove the bot works, but the record supports reading this as a risky trading-tool demonstration with disclosed limitations rather than a promise that every viewer will profit.

citations.quote: If you fund the contract with 0.4 BNB or less and the bot targets another token with high burn fees the contract will basically waste in fees more than making a profit.
I recommend funding the contract with around 1 - 0.5 BNB just to make sure that won't happen.
I've had really good luck with this last few weeks I've made several hundred BNB
which I can show the transaction reports on BSCscan to corroborate that.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution is right that viewers are shown how to fund and activate a contract. But those steps establish what the demonstration asks viewers to do, not that the contract diverts funds or that the speaker conceals all downside. Its own description expressly says fees can exceed profit. Nor does the statement that buying and selling is automatic independently establish that the claimed returns occurred.

citations.quote: the contract will basically waste in fees more than making a profit.
It automatically buys and sells for you.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The fee warning is narrow: it attributes possible losses to insufficient funding and recommends putting more BNB into the contract. It does not verify the contract's code or the claimed returns. The speaker still instructs viewers to transfer funds, activate the contract, and expect automated payouts; the account of having made hundreds of BNB remains the speaker's own claim.

opening.argument: Judge, the video follows an operational tutorial from creating a file in Remix through compilation, wallet connection, deployment, and checking the contract address on BSCscan. The sampled views likewise show the editor, compiler, deployment controls, and wallet transaction dialogs. The speaker's account of profit is part of the demonstration, but those concrete programming and deployment steps are substantial content in their own right. Classifying the entire video by its return claim overlooks what a viewer is actually being walked through: a smart-contract workflow whose claimed performance is not independently established by the material.

citations.quote: under contracts i'm going to create a new contract which is with this new file create new file icon on the top left.
let me go compile front-run bot there we go it compiled so we're gonna deploy this to our wallet
I copy that, paste it in BSC scan, we can see that it's an address there now.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution cites funding, activation, and automated trading, all of which fit the demonstrated workflow. It does not follow from those steps alone that the video shows a confirmed fraudulent transfer or verified profit. The tutorial's visible compiler and wallet stages matter when assessing its primary presentation, even though they cannot establish that the contract is safe.

citations.quote: Next thing that we do, after it's sent to the contract, we'll just go over here and press the action button

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The deployment walkthrough is the means by which viewers are directed to fund the contract. Compilation and an address appearing on BSCscan do not show that its trading logic works or that funds will return. The speaker explicitly ties activation to automated trades and a claimed 90% payout, then presents a large return as the result. Technical detail does not remove the video's financial solicitation.

citations.quote: we're just gonna send some funds to that contract
It automatically buys and sells for you.
Yeah, it's already around 15X.

opening.argument: Judge, the described transaction is a user deploying a contract through Remix, connecting their own wallet, and sending funds to the contract address they just created. The supplied record does not identify a credential request, a recruitment chain, or a third-party account receiving the transfer. It also does not independently establish where the funded contract ultimately sends its balance. The high return claims deserve scrutiny, but the evidence for the mechanics of theft is missing; the observed workflow can be read as use of a trading tool rather than a demonstrated diversion to the creator.

citations.quote: so we're gonna deploy this to our wallet
we're just gonna send some funds to that contract that we just created
make sure I got the right address in there

rebuttal.rebuttal: Funding a contract is not, by itself, evidence that the speaker receives the funds. The prosecution's quoted transfer and action steps establish an attempted use of a deployed contract, while the front-running description states the speaker's purported trading purpose. The supplied material does not trace the contract's later balance or independently verify the promised payout, so neither outcome can be treated as established.

citations.quote: we're just gonna send some funds to that contract that we just created
it will front-run all the retail investors that come in

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A visible credential request or identified recipient is not required to recognize the risk in this pitch. Viewers are directed to paste supplied contract code, fund the deployed contract, and trigger it on the strength of asserted automated returns. The record does not verify the contract's behavior, while the title and narration make unusually large profit claims. Calling the wallet and contract the viewer's own does not establish who controls the code's effects or where funds ultimately go.
